newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kissei says US clinical test of HIV drug to start.
newsitem.headline: Kissei says US clinical test of HIV drug to start.

text.p: Kissei Pharmaceutical Co Ltd said on Friday that the AIDS Clinical Trial Group of the United States would start phase two clinical trials of an HIV drug, paving the way for Kissei's development of the drug in Japan.
Development of the drug, a protease inhibitor, which blocks the virus from attacking cells, was initiated by U.S. drug firm Vertex Pharmaceuticals Inc.
Kissei recently finished phase one of the three stages of clinical tests of the drug, called KVX-478, in Japan, a spokesman for the company said.

It will wait for the result of the phase two clinical trial in the United States, which is expected to start in October and be completed at the end of 1997, before deciding to go on with its clinical trials in Japan, the spokesman said.
The AIDS Clinical Trial Group is a network of clinical testing institutions in the United States and is publicly subsidised.

Glaxo Wellcome Plc has finished phase one and two clinical trials in Europe and the United States to assess the efficacy of the drug when used in combination with other HIV drugs, Kissei said in a statement.
